items.title: 1.6 million affected by Bhotekoshi floods, says government report
items.summary: Government’s first situation report puts the death toll at 1,050, with nearly 4,000 missing and more than 21,000 security personnel involved in a vast rescue operation alongside international teams.

items.title: UN Women estimates 43,000 women and girls in Nepal need urgent flood assistance
items.summary: An estimated 157,050 women and girls in Rasuwa and Nuwakot have been directly or indirectly affected, with food, safe water and protection emerging as urgent concerns.

items.title: Local governments take charge of flood relief after criticism of centralised response
items.summary: Six-party committees have been formed in Rasuwa and Nuwakot to coordinate relief distribution as the government faces criticism over its initial reliance on security agencies.

items.title: Nepal Prime Minister: Bhotekoshi flood was one of region’s largest disasters
items.summary: The incident indicates that the risks Nepal face in the Himalayan region are increasing alongside climate change.

items.title: What is the progress in the search for workers trapped in Nepal’s flooded hydropowers?
items.summary: Rescue teams have located tunnel entrances and advanced hundreds of metres into several hydropower projects along the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli corridor as the search for missing workers continues.

items.title: They survived the flood. Their families did not.
items.summary: From a Rasuwa holding centre, survivors recount desperate escapes, relatives swept away and the loss of homes, villages and entire families in the Bhotekoshi disaster.

items.title: Nepal flood death toll rises to 987, nearly 4,000 still missing
items.summary: The latest toll comes as search teams recover bodies from Rasuwa and downstream districts, while hundreds of workers at hydropower projects remain unaccounted for.

items.title: Nepal seeks urgent climate finance after Bhotekoshi flood
items.summary: Government asks global loss-and-damage fund for immediate support, saying the scale of destruction exceeds the country’s capacity to respond.

items.title: Hundreds missing, billions in goods feared lost in Bhotekoshi flood
items.summary: Traders, drivers and customs workers remain unaccounted for six days after the flood swept through the Rasuwa border area, while officials struggle to determine how many cargo containers and how much merchandise were lost.

items.title: Fourteen minutes before the flood hit, a warning sent 900 students running for safety
items.summary: A frantic warning from a school accountant, relayed by relatives in flood-hit Rasuwa, gave teachers just minutes to evacuate Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School before a wall of mud and water tore through Bidur, destroying the school and sweeping away homes and bridges.

items.title: Flood rescue enters critical days, anxious families hope missing loved ones are alive
items.summary: Hundreds of hydropower workers and staff remain missing across projects in Rasuwa and Nuwakot after the August 26 Bhotekoshi flood.

items.title: ‘I managed to survive, but my brother and sister couldn’t’
items.summary: 14-year-old Akash Tamang says he survived the floods, but his younger brother and sister are missing. 17,000 children have been directly affected by floods in Bhotekoshi and Trishuli corridors, says UNICEF.

items.title: RSP chair Lamichhane briefs President Paudel on Bhotekoshi flood response
items.summary: Lamichhane also met Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Monday to take stock of the government’s search, rescue and relief efforts.

items.title: More countries join Nepal flood rescue efforts
items.summary: Assistance ranges from tunnel rescue and forensic expertise to relief materials and specialised equipment. Nepal seeks more help for recovery and reconstruction.

items.title: Bhotekoshi flood survivors face new battle against illness
items.summary: Medicines are running short, health services remain disrupted, and crowded shelters are raising fears of disease outbreaks among displaced families.

items.title: China closes Tatopani border point citing landslides risk
items.summary: With Tatopani closed and Rasuwagadhi destroyed by floods, Nepal’s traders are now left with Korala as the only functioning overland trade route with China ahead of the festive season.

items.title: Four bodies swept away by Bhotekoshi floods found in India
items.summary: Indian police hand over the bodies recovered from a river in India’s Maharajganj district to Nepal Police.

items.title: Death toll from Bhotekoshi flood reaches 903
items.summary: Government figures show 4,247 people remain unaccounted for, including 592 foreign nationals, as search and identification efforts continue in the flood-hit districts.

items.title: From hospital to hospital, families search for the ones the flood took
items.summary: Relatives travel hundreds of kilometres across Nepal, moving between morgues, rescue camps and social media in search of any sign of those swept away or trapped by the Bhotekoshi flood.
